system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the STRUCTURE OF A CORPORATE TRANSACTION AT
CLOSING. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from public primary sources
(SEC filings, company releases, reputable press). This slice describes ONLY how the
deal was structured -- what crossed the ownership boundary and what did not -- at
the moment of closing. You are DELIBERATELY NOT shown what happened to the combined
company afterward, and you must NOT speculate about later outcomes, success, or
failure. Code STRICTLY the deal as structured. If the slice does not let you
determine a field, you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from
outside knowledge of the companies.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

A. BUNDLE SIGNATURE -- for each of six organizational tiers, classify what happened
to that tier when the transaction crossed the ownership boundary. Exactly one label
per tier.
  T1 Owner Intent (controlling principal / imprint).
     Labels: replace, imprint-share, continue, terminate, reconstruct, replicate, mutual-replace, uncertain.
       replace = old controlling intent exited, a new one installed;
       imprint-share = both principals' intent co-present;
       continue = same controlling intent persists;
       terminate = the controlling intent ended with no successor;
       reconstruct = intent re-formed into a new (often non-commercial) purpose;
       replicate = intent copied into a standardized template (e.g. franchising);
       mutual-replace = two intents fused into a jointly-new one (merger of equals).
  T2 Business Model, T3 Business Entity (legal vehicle), T4 Product (customer-
  acceptance layer), T5 Process (operations), T6 Organization (people/culture).
     Labels for T2-T6: 1-1, N-1, 1-N, subset, partial, read-only, swap, terminate, null, uncertain.
       1-1 = transferred whole, one-to-one; N-1 = many collapsed into one;
       1-N = one split into many; subset = only part transferred;
       partial = transferred but incompletely / with friction;
       read-only = licensed / accessed without ownership transfer;
       swap = exchanged for a different one (e.g. new legal domicile);
       terminate = ended; null = not applicable / nothing at this tier.

B. TIER-TRANSFER GAPS -- code strictly from the STRUCTURE OF THE DEAL AT CLOSING.
A gap is a STRUCTURAL MISMATCH IN WHAT THE DEAL TRANSFERRED, not a later failure.
  gap_45: Did the customer-facing product/asset (T4, what customers buy) cross the
    ownership boundary WITHOUT the operational processes that produce or deliver it
    (T5) transferring or being aligned coherently alongside it? A documented
    product-vs-process structural mismatch AT CLOSING. 1 = yes such a gap; 0 = no
    (product and its processes moved together, or neither moved); uncertain.
  gap_56: Did the operational processes (T5) transfer or get re-engineered WITHOUT
    the organization / people / management / culture that run them (T6) transferring
    or aligning coherently alongside, AT CLOSING? 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  gap_mitigated: If (and only if) you coded a structural gap above, was that gap
    documented as contractually absorbed at closing via a transitional-services or
    operating agreement allocating the shared substrate? yes / no / NA (NA if no gap).

E. collapse_state: Any Tier-1 fusion documented in the deal structure? none /
   T1=T4 (founder identity IS the product) / T1=T3 (the legal subject IS a specific
   natural person) / T1=T3=T4 / T1=T2 / T1=T6 / uncertain.

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your gap_45 and gap_56
codes specifically. Cite ONLY closing-structure evidence; do NOT reason about later
outcomes.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: inability to determine a
structural field is "uncertain"; a gap you cannot document at closing is 0.

# Structural sub-dossier — Freeport-McMoRan Inc. / PT Freeport Indonesia, Grasberg-area ownership and joint-venture arrangements at closing

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. This sub-dossier describes ONLY how the
> transaction was structured at closing — what crossed the ownership boundary and what
> did not. It contains no post-transaction outcome information.

## Note on the drawn filing
- The drawn accession (0001193125-14-413217, Form 8-K filed 2014-11-14) reports that on
  November 10, 2014, Freeport-McMoRan Inc. ("FCX"), as issuer, and Freeport-McMoRan Oil &
  Gas LLC, as guarantor, entered an Underwriting Agreement for $3.0 billion of Senior
  Notes across four tranches, proceeds earmarked to repay outstanding debt; this is a
  debt-financing filing and does not itself document a joint-venture or ownership
  transaction. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-14-413217, Form 8-K]

## Parties and ownership structure (closing era, FY2014 10-K)
The facts below are drawn from the registrant's contemporaneous 2014 filings that
document its Indonesia ownership/joint-venture arrangement.
- PT Freeport Indonesia ("PT-FI") is an Indonesian limited liability company; FCX directly
  owns 81.28 percent of its outstanding common stock and indirectly owns a further 9.36
  percent through wholly owned subsidiary PT Indocopper Investama, with the Indonesian
  government owning the remaining 9.36 percent. [SRC: SEC accession 0000831259-15-000016, Form 10-K (FY2014)]
- PT-FI has an unincorporated joint venture with Rio Tinto plc ("Rio Tinto"), under which
  Rio Tinto holds a 40 percent interest in certain assets and in future production above
  specified annual amounts of copper, gold and silver through 2021 in Block A of PT-FI's
  Contract of Work (COW), and 40 percent of all Block A production after 2021; FCX and its
  predecessors have been the only operator of Block A since 1967, and PT-FI's share of
  copper production/sales was 98 percent in 2014 — Rio Tinto's interest is a cash-flow
  entitlement above thresholds, not an operating role. [SRC: SEC accession 0000831259-15-000016, Form 10-K (FY2014)]

## Contemporaneous regulatory/structural event — the July 2014 MOU
- On July 25, 2014, PT-FI entered a Memorandum of Understanding ("MOU") with Indonesia's
  Directorate General of Mineral and Coal and Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources to
  negotiate, over the following six months, an amended COW addressing concession size,
  royalties/taxes, domestic processing, divestment, local content, and post-2021
  continuation of operations. [SRC: SEC accession 0000831259-14-000039, Form 8-K (event date 2014-07-25)]
- Effective with signing, PT-FI agreed to pay new export duties, provide a $115 million
  assurance bond for smelter development, and raise royalties to 4.0 percent copper / 3.75
  percent gold (from 3.5 / 1.0 percent), enabling resumption of concentrate exports from
  August 2014; items reserved for the COW negotiation included cost-shared smelter/
  refining development and provisions for FCX to divest up to an additional 20.64
  percentage points (30 percent total) to the Indonesian government/nationals at fair
  value, with operations continuing 2022-2041. Under the MOU, no other COW terms were to
  change until the amended COW was completed. [SRC: SEC accession 0000831259-14-000039, Form 8-K]

## What crossed the boundary / what stayed at closing
- Operating control of Grasberg remained with FCX/PT-FI as sole historical operator; the
  MOU restructured fiscal terms and opened a path toward a larger government ownership
  share but did not itself transfer operating control, management, or the workforce
  running PT-FI's mining operations. [SRC: SEC accession 0000831259-14-000039, Form 8-K; SEC accession 0000831259-15-000016, Form 10-K (FY2014)]
- The customer-facing product (copper/gold/silver production and concentrate) continued
  to be produced and sold by PT-FI under the existing COW; the Rio Tinto joint venture
  affected only sharing of production/cash flows above thresholds, not which entity
  produced. [SRC: SEC accession 0000831259-15-000016, Form 10-K (FY2014)]
- The legal vehicle (PT-FI operating under its COW) was retained at closing; the MOU
  contemplated only a future COW amendment, not its replacement or a new incorporated
  joint-venture entity at this stage. [SRC: SEC accession 0000831259-14-000039, Form 8-K]

## Structural summary (closing only)
- At the 2014 closing point the Grasberg-area structure comprised FCX's 90.64 percent
  combined direct-and-indirect equity in PT-FI, the Indonesian government's 9.36 percent,
  and a separate unincorporated Rio Tinto production/cash-flow-sharing joint venture over
  Block A, with the July 2014 MOU opening a fiscal and prospective-divestment
  renegotiation without altering, at that time, who operated the mine, produced the
  product, or managed the business. [SRC: SEC accession 0000831259-15-000016, Form 10-K (FY2014); SEC accession 0000831259-14-000039, Form 8-K]

[SLICE END]
